S2 [fact]: squash must return an empty string for null and undefined and retain TypeError for numbers and objects. S8 [fact/open: Q11]: Doc comments must follow the Orchard style guide, whose authoritative location is unverified. S9 [fact]: Preserve squash behavior for all existing string inputs exactly. S10 [fact]: Add tests in the existing node:test and node:assert style. S11 [fact/open: Q10]: Support a million-record workload with straightforward code and no premature optimization; a numerical performance bound is unspecified. Boundaries [fact]: This intake only reads the working-directory project, implements nothing, changes no files, and starts no server; it authorizes no additional scope. Runtime [fact]: The existing entry point is the CommonJS export in src/text.js and npm test runs node --test. Visibility [fact/assumption]: The isolated source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return; the assumed checkout delivery becomes usable after the completed result is returned, while any deployed target would only contain it after release. Discovery leads [hints, not verified facts]: repository files and history if available, legacy trim helper and callers, real-export schemas or examples if authorized, the Orchard team's workspace, channels, internal documentation or private repositories, and the relevant owners; no specific channel, site, repository, or owner has been established. Keep sensitive locators only in an authorized private store, never in KNOWLEDGE/. This is a library helper, not an interactive product; interactive actor and session questions do not apply.
